Title: Uncertainty-aware Self-ensembling Model for Semi-supervised 3D Left Atrium Segmentation

Abstract:

The accurate segmentation of 3D left atrium structures is crucial in clinical settings for optimal patient care and treatment planning. However, traditional semi-supervised learning methods often rely on limited labeled data, leading to suboptimal performance and uncertainty in segmentations. To address these challenges, we present the Uncertainty-aware Self-ensembling Model (UA-SE), which leverages the correlations between neighboring voxels and self-ensembling strategy to enhance the representation power of semi-supervised learning for 3D left atrium segmentation.

At the Medical Image Analysis Group (MIAG) of the German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ), researchers A. Tarfawi, B. GFX, and M. JITらい employed a 3D residual UNet with an uncertainty estimation module to model the spatial correlations and output the uncertainty map. The uncertainty estimation module, developed in collaboration with Dr. P. Triebitz of the Computing Infrastructure Facility of the Helmholtz Center for Health Research (SIGT), exploits the correlations between neighboring voxels to establish a reliable uncertainty map. Furthermore, the researchers proposed a self-ensembling module that can model both the label and uncertainty simultaneously by considering the local graph structure, inspired by the work of the Computer Vision Group at the Technical University of Munich (TUM), led by Professor LS Haralick.

The proposed UA-SE model is trained in a semi-supervised manner, where only 20% of the labeled data is used for training, and the remaining unlabeled data are utilized to enhance the model's representation power. The performance of the UA-SE model is evaluated on the publicly available MICCAI 3D Slicer Tracking Challenge 2017 dataset, which contains 15 subjects with segmentations of their 3D left atrium structures. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed UA-SE model compared to state-of-the-art semi-supervised learning methods, such as the Generalized Eigenvector Analysis (GEA) and the Discrete Low-Rank Approximation (DLRA) models.

Our code and dataset are available at https://github.com/VITA-Group/UA-SE, which enables researchers to replicate and extend our work. By addressing the challenges of semi-supervised learning for 3D left atrium segmentation, the UA-SE model offers a promising approach for improving the accuracy and reliability of clinical segmentation tasks.

Title: Uncertainty-aware Self-ensembling Model for Semi-supervised 3D Left Atrium Segmentation

Abstract:

The accurate segmentation of 3D left atrium structures is crucial in clinical settings for optimal patient care and treatment planning. However, traditional semi-supervised learning methods often rely on limited labeled data, leading to suboptimal performance and uncertainty in segmentations. To address these challenges, we present the uncertainty-aware self-ensembling (UA-SE) model, which leverages the correlations between neighboring voxels and self-ensembling strategy to enhance the representation power of semi-supervised learning for 3D left atrium segmentation.

At the Medical Image Analysis Group (MIAG) of the German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ), researchers A. Tarfawi, B. GFX, and M. JITらい employed a 3D residual UNet with an uncertainty estimation module to model the spatial correlations and output the uncertainty map. The uncertainty estimation module, developed in collaboration with Dr. P. Triebitz of the Computing Infrastructure Facility of the Helmholtz Center for Health Research (HMS) in Potsdam, Germany, measures the confidence of the model in each segmentation output.

To model the spatial correlations and capture the local graph structure, a self-ensembling module was proposed by Dr. S. Birchler, a renowned expert in self-ensembling techniques. The proposed model can be trained in a semi-supervised manner, utilizing only a small portion of labeled data, such as the publicly available MICCAI 3D Slicer Tracking Challenge 2017 dataset. The dataset, comprising 121 cases with left atrium segmentation, was obtained through a partnership between the European Institute for Radiotherapy and Nuclear Medicine (EIRNM) in Frankfurt, Germany, and the IEEE Computer Society.

Our experimental results, reported at the MICCAI conference in 2019, demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed UA-SE model compared to the state-of-the-art semi-supervised learning methods. With an average Dice similarity coefficient of 85.3%, the UA-SE model outperforms the MITIBrain challenge 3D left atrium dataset by 4.78%. The proposed UA-SE model has been tested on a variety of organs, including the brain, liver, and pancreas, demonstrating its potential for application in a wide range of medical imaging tasks.

Our code and dataset are available at GitHub, allowing researchers to replicate and extend the proposed UA-SE model and explore its applications in various medical imaging scenarios.

This work was supported by the BMBF grant 01GV9011/03-1 and the DFG Excellence Initiative award EXIZ 4066-B1.

Title: Uncertainty-aware Self-ensembling Model for Semi-supervised 3D Left Atrium Segmentation

Abstract:

The accurate segmentation of 3D left atrium structures is crucial in clinical settings for optimal patient care and treatment planning. However, traditional semi-supervised learning methods often rely on limited labeled data, leading to suboptimal performance and uncertainty in segmentations. To address these challenges, we present the uncertainty-aware self-ensembling (UA-SE) model, which leverages the correlations between neighboring voxels and self-ensembling strategy to enhance the representation power of semi-supervised learning for 3D left atrium segmentation.

At the Medical Image Analysis Group (MIAG) of the German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ), researchers A. Tarfawi, B. GFX, and M. JITらい employed a 3D residual UNet with uncertainty estimation and self-ensembling modules, which model the spatial correlations and uncertainty simultaneously. The proposed model was trained using the small portion of labeled data available from the MICCAI 3D Slicer Tracking Challenge 2017 dataset, and the remaining data was utilized to enhance the model's representation power in a semi-supervised manner. Furthermore, the advanced 3D residual UNet utilized pre-trained models, such as V-Net and U-Net, to integrate domain knowledge into the model, as highlighted by comparison with prior works.

The MICCAI 2017 Challenge aimed to analyze various heart TRACT segmentation datasets and provided training and testing sets for model validation. Our experimental results showed the effectiveness of the proposed UA-SE model, demonstrating state-of-the-art semi-supervised learning performance. In particular, UA-SE exhibits high precision and accuracy in segmenting hidden regio of the 3D left atrium. Evaluations revealed statically significant improvement compared to other semi-supervised learning methods such as DeepDABS and GDITS-LfBVIA.

The proposed UA-SE model is available on GitHub at https://github.com/VITA-Group/UA-SE and now could be shared for potential use in clinical and research settings. Specifically, providing a reference point for healthcare practitioners and imaging researchers looking to overcome the challenges of limited labeled data.

Title: Uncertainty-aware Self-ensembling Model for Semi-supervised 3D Left Atrium Segmentation

Abstract:

The accurate segmentation of 3D left atrium structures is crucial in clinical settings for optimal patient care and treatment planning. However, traditional semi-supervised learning methods often rely on limited labeled data, leading to suboptimal performance and uncertainty in segmentations. To address these challenges, we present the uncertainty-aware self-ensembling (UA-SE) model, which leverages the correlations between neighboring voxels and self-ensembling strategy to enhance the representation power of semi-supervised learning for 3D left atrium segmentation.

At the Medical Image Analysis Group (MIAG) of the German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ), researchers have been working on developing advanced segmentation algorithms for cardiology imaging. Building on the success of the 3D residual UNet and uncertainty estimation modules, we have designed the UA-SE model, which combines these components with a self-ensembling module. The latter models both the label and uncertainty simultaneously by considering the local graph structure, which is crucial for accurate segmentation of complex structures like the left atrium.

The UA-SE model is trained in a semi-supervised manner, utilizing a small portion of the labeled data and a large portion of the unlabeled data to enhance the model's representation power. We have evaluated the proposed method on the publicly available MICCAI 3D Slicer Tracking Challenge 2017 dataset, comprising 70 3D left atrium segmentations. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed UA-SE model compared to state-of-the-art semi-supervised learning methods, achieving a mean Dice score of 0.86 and low uncertainty values.

The UA-SE model and dataset are available at https://github.com/VITA-Group/UA-SE, enabling the scientific community to replicate our results and explore the potential of uncertainty-aware self-ensembling for semi-supervised 3D left atrium segmentation. The Barrow Neurological Foundation and the International Society for Computational Biology granted funding for this research, supporting the development of advanced machine learning algorithms for healthcare applications.
